items.title: William Ballariel Interview, 1959-10-02
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I'm wondering if you can tell us, Mr. Ballero, about the music when you first began playing.

ctx.x: No, it takes quite a while. You can see that we had plenty of work, you see, according to that book.

Let's see, as the years go on here, sometimes the pay is going up a little bit too. There's more $6 dates here for some of the parties. Up to $6.25 quite often here. That's in the summer too. I'm wondering if you can tell us, Mr. Ballero, about the music when you first began playing. When you were a boy, before you joined any brass band, what was the dance music like here in Mobile? As far back as you can remember, did they have bands with blowing instruments or just strings? What kind of a band did they use?

Well, I think there were a few orchestras around there, but not really. The old time when the boys were coming up, they had most of what they called string bands. It would be string instruments with about maybe four, five, six pieces. But in the late years, after the Excelsior Band, well, during the Excelsior Band, about, I say about 20 years ago, they began to get orchestras together. The fellas began to organize good string orchestras, you see. They'd have pianos and trumpets and clarinet and violins and bass…
